messages:
raj: FYI CA tried to scale down gpu-pool-usw2-3 and got blocked by PDBs, nodes still draining and cost is spiking.
ashley: Noticed the same — autoscaler log shows "would violate PDB" for model-serving-* replicas.
miguel: Can you paste the autoscaler log line? I want to see which PDBs are preventing eviction.
kube-bot: cluster-autoscaler: node gpu-node-42: removal skipped: pod model-serving-replicaset-6d4f blocked by PodDisruptionBudget 'model-serving-pdb' (minAvailable=2)
raj: Exact. These are long-lived GPU pods with PDB minAvailable: 2. There aren't spare GPU nodes for reschedule so CA leaves nodes.
ashley: Two immediate options: reduce PDB strictness (use maxUnavailable) or mark some pods safe-to-evict so CA can move them during scale down.
miguel: Agreed. For quick mitigation we can annotate non-critical canaries and batch jobs with:
```bash
kubectl annotate pod <pod> cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=true
```
That makes CA ignore PDBs for those pods when evicting.
raj: Small correction — CA still respects PDBs unless pods themselves are annotated safe-to-evict. Annotation is per-pod; we should automate for ReplicaSets with a label selector.
sam (oncall): Is it safe to do that automatically for all model-serving pods? We don't want to accidentally evict primary-replica holding GPU session state.
miguel: No — target only canaries and stateless workers. Plan:
- add label team=canary to canary RS
- controller script to annotate pods with label team=canary
- update docs and runbook

ashley: Also consider switching PDBs from minAvailable to maxUnavailable: for example `maxUnavailable: 1` allows one pod to be taken down and is CA-friendly.
raj: True but careful: maxUnavailable on stateful sets can be risky. For Deployments it's fine.
miguel: I'll open a small K8s Job that patches pods on node drain. Example script snippet:
```sh
# pre-drain helper
for p in $(kubectl get pods -l team=canary -o name); do
  kubectl annotate $p cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=true --overwrite
done
kubectl drain $NODE --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --grace-period=120
```
ashley: Nice. Also add a short TTL so annotation is removed after reschedule to avoid long-term side effects.
sam (oncall): Operationally: we need a guardrail in CA settings: set scaleDownUnneededTime to 15m for gpu pools and scale-down-utilization threshold to 0.2. Prevents thrash.
raj: Good call. Also add capacity-aware routing in scheduler: prefer placing moveable pods to nodes with other moveable pods so drains are cheaper.
miguel: I'll PR the runbook: "gpu-pool-soft-drain-and-safe-evict" with steps: identify blocking PDBs, label canaries, annotate safe-to-evict, adjust PDBs where safe, adjust CA config for gpu pools, and rollback steps.
ashley: Can you include exact kubectl commands + the CA config snippet?
miguel: Yup. I'll push the PR and run the on-call patch during quiet hours. Tagging @sam for rollout window.
sam (oncall): ACK. Schedule between 02:00-04:00 UTC. :thumbsup:
raj: Thanks team. After PR we should run a dry-run: `kubectl drain --dry-run=client` and CA simulate logs to ensure no surprises.
miguel: Will do and post the link to the PR here.
kube-bot: deploy-bot: added ticket RN-2487 to changelog: "gpu soft drain - safe-to-evict automation"
